_readme: The research catalogue (R2): every discovery the city's schools can make, which field researches it, what it unlocks, history's date, what it needs first and what the work costs.

Read by ResearchCatalog. The file is packaged with the game, so a change here needs a rebuild. 89 entries: the first study's 40 (research-design.md 4), the 1900 study's 48 (research-1900.md 8.1-8.4) and L5 (research-1900.md 8.6).

CODE IS PERMANENT. buildings.json's "since" names a discovery by its code ("E1", "PE14") and saves will key by it. Never renumber or reuse a code; a new discovery takes the next free number in its field.
Reordering entries is safe. The order here is the order the studies print them in.
code      the study's code: E, M, B, L (the 1951-1995 catalogue) and PE, PM, PB, PL (before 1950, "P" for pre); L5 is the 1966 pension contribution.
name      the study's Discovery column.
field     ENGINEERING, MEDICINE, BUSINESS or LAW: the school that researches it (the Institute of technology, the Medical school, the Business school, the Law school).
kind      one or two of "building", "equipment", "recipe", "drug": what it unlocks.
kindNote  optional: what a recipe is when it is not a production recipe ("a Policy lever", "a Policy dial", "a market rule", "a sentencing option").
size      what the work is like, one of building, equipment, recipe, drug (a Walk-in Clinic is a recipe's work though it is a building; a vaccine or a drug carries clinical trials).

year, month, monthKnown   history's date. The month is the study's where its World column names one (monthKnown true); where it names none, the study's model puts the discovery in June or the month the model chose (monthKnown false).
The law rows (PL1-PL12, L5) carry exactly the dates of PolicyDates.java, which the Policy gate reads: a lever dated by the year alone opens in January. L1-L4 are not levers.
world     the study's World column: the date and place.
touches   what it touches: the buildings it changes (medicine: the mechanism it changes; law: where in Policy).
effect    the study's Effect column, in the study's figures; "(est.)" and "(unverified)" are the study's.
sources   the study's source keys for the effect, as the study brackets them.
needs     the codes of the discoveries it needs first (an earlier or same-month date; ResearchCatalog reports one that is later or unknown).
requires  what else it needs, in words (a coast, a magnetite field), or "".

fee       whether it would carry a licence fee while under patent (research-design.md 2.4: 25% of what it adds, 20 years); feeNote is the study's qualifier. Law is not patented: every law row is false.

work      researcher-years at its date. The tables' figure; for the PL rows and L5, which the tables do not print, the rule: 400 (building, equipment), 200 (recipe) or 500 (drug) at 1950, times 1.053 a year (1.035 a year in medicine) to the year, rounded.
study     the section it comes from.

entries.name: Oxygen converter
entries.effect: a heat in under 40 min, from 10-12 h; 50-55 Nm3 of oxygen a tonne
entries.requires: hot iron from a blast furnace

entries.name: Preheater kiln
entries.effect: fuel 7.0 GJ (wet) to 3.0-3.6 GJ a tonne of clinker

entries.name: Jack-up drilling rig
entries.effect: deepest water 30 m to 120-150 m

entries.name: Taconite pellets
entries.effect: 30-35% Fe rock to 65% Fe pellets

entries.name: Shipping container
entries.effect: loading US$5.83 to 0.16 a tonne; 1.7 to 30 t an hour a docker; turnaround 3 weeks to 18 h with the gantry crane (1959)

entries.name: Flash desalination
entries.effect: fresh water from the sea at 13.5-25.5 kWh a m3

entries.name: Hydrocracking
entries.effect: gas oil into about 107% of its volume as jet and diesel

entries.name: Welding robot
entries.touches: Vehicle Works, Assembly Plant, Commercial Vehicle Plant
entries.effect: torch working 90% of the time, from 30%

entries.name: Continuous caster
entries.touches: Steel Shop, Electric Arc Furnace, Mini-Mill
entries.effect: +10-12% steel from the same melt; -10-15% labour; -1 MBtu a ton direct; US$40-80 per tonne a year (1978)

entries.name: Semi-dwarf wheat
entries.effect: yields about doubled in five years, with fertiliser

entries.name: Zeolite catalyst
entries.effect: petrol 55.5 to 62.0% of the feed; coke 5.6 to 4.1%

entries.name: Leaching and electrowinning
entries.effect: cathode from ore under 1% Cu, 60-70% recovered

entries.name: Scrap mini-mill
entries.effect: ~400 kWh a tonne from scrap; US$140-200 per tonne a year against ~1,000 integrated

entries.name: Mechanised harvesting
entries.effect: 3.8x the wood a worker of a Logging Camp (the materials study's figures)

entries.name: Longwall shields
entries.effect: 30 to 149 t a face worker a day (1975-89); 60% to 80% of the seam

entries.name: Wind farm
entries.effect: Altamont's 1986 farms ran at about 9% of capacity (est.); projects built 1998-2003 run at 23%, 2013-21 at 40%

entries.name: Double-stack rail
entries.effect: twice the containers a train

entries.name: Thin-slab caster
entries.effect: flat steel from scrap; reheating 2.0 to 0.5-0.8 MBtu a tonne

entries.name: TB drugs
entries.touches: the year-or-more slot of Sickness' ring recovers
entries.effect: Canadian TB beds 18,977 to 9,722 in ten years; stays 362 to 224 days

entries.name: Breathing machine (ICU)
entries.touches: fewer of the served long-sick die; more COLLEGE_HEALTH a bed
entries.effect: respiratory polio deaths 87% to about 22%

entries.name: Polio vaccine
entries.touches: summer outbreaks lose their polio share; fewer enter the long-sick pool disabled
entries.effect: US paralytic cases -90% in 5 years, -99.7% in 10; Canada 1953: about 9,000 cases, 494 deaths

entries.name: Kidney dialysis
entries.touches: a death becomes a patient: 3 four-hour sessions a week
entries.effect: about 6 patients a station (est.); US patients 78,000 (1984) to 187,000 (1994)

entries.name: Hip replacement
entries.touches: general-care stays shorter; more recover in senior care
entries.effect: stay about 30 days, 9.1 by 1991, 3.7 by 2008; discharged to care 17.8% to 34.3%

entries.name: CT scanner
entries.touches: fewer needless operations: general care's capacity up
entries.effect: per 100 suspected appendicitis, 13 operations and 50 bed-days avoided

entries.name: Angioplasty
entries.touches: heart patients back to work sooner; fewer deaths
entries.effect: back at work at 2 months 40% against 10%; deaths 9% to 7%

entries.name: Assisted living
entries.touches: a senior who needs help but not a nursing bed
entries.effect: a new senior-care place

entries.name: Keyhole and day surgery
entries.touches: 3 fewer days in a bed and 22.5 fewer off work; 35% more operations
entries.effect: laparoscopic share <1% to 92% in ten years (Ontario)

entries.name: Statins
entries.touches: coronary deaths and hospital days fall
entries.effect: deaths 11.5% to 8.2% over 5.4 years; hospital days -34%

entries.name: Business computer
entries.touches: Commercial Bank, Shared Services, Contact Centre
entries.effect: posting 245 to 33,000 accounts an hour; -25% of the clerks it touches, +29 computer posts an office

entries.name: Call distributor
entries.effect: one queue for every line: 23-37% fewer agents for the same calls (est., Erlang C)

entries.name: Cash machine
entries.effect: tellers a branch 20 to 13; branches +43%

entries.name: Walk-in clinic
entries.effect: a doctor without an appointment

entries.name: Barcode scanner
entries.touches: grocery and convenience stores, filling stations
entries.effect: store payroll -5.35%; about 8 years' payback at 1974 prices

entries.name: Shared services
entries.effect: one back office for many firms

entries.name: Lean production
entries.effect: 26.5 to 19.1 hours a vehicle; inventory 96 to 81 days

entries.name: Online shop
entries.effect: e-commerce 0.6% to 17.1% of US retail in 27 years

entries.name: Deposit insurance
entries.touches: the bank: insured deposits do not run
entries.effect: US bank failures 1,350-4,000 a year (1930-33) to 9 (1934)

entries.name: Reorganisation
entries.touches: a business that cannot pay keeps its plant under a stay
entries.effect: kept as a going concern 80% of the time against 63-71%; 77 cents on the dollar in rich countries

entries.name: Electronic monitoring
entries.touches: Jail and Penitentiary beds; the offender keeps working
entries.effect: re-arrest 22% to 13%; custody costs 3.9x supervision

entries.name: DNA evidence
entries.effect: reoffending -42% within a year; 1% more detection, over 2% less crime

entries.name: Electric arc steel furnace
entries.world: Dec 1900, France (Heroult); North America 5 Apr 1906, Syracuse (1907 by another source)
entries.effect: steel from scrap by electricity, not fuel: a 3-t heat on a 500 kW supply (1906); early kWh a tonne not found

entries.name: High-speed tool steel
entries.touches: Machine Works, Fabrication Shop, Fabrication Works
entries.effect: cutting speed 30 to 90 ft a minute

entries.name: Rotary drilling
entries.effect: soft-rock and salt-dome fields: one well about 100,000 bbl a day; Spindletop 20% of US output in 1902 (est.)

entries.name: Long rotary kiln
entries.touches: Cement Plant, Large Cement Plant, Lime Kiln
entries.effect: kilns 60-80 ft to up to 150 ft; about 30 t a day a kiln (1900) to 680 t (1950); coal a tonne about the same

entries.name: Rapid sand filter
entries.effect: 60 times the slow-sand rate, so about 1/60 the filter land (est.); typhoid deaths -36% to -46% (two studies, three readings)

entries.name: Steam-turbine station
entries.effect: station efficiency about 3.6% (1900) toward 24.3% (1950) with PE16: 100 to 14.8 MJ of coal a kWh (est.)

entries.name: Froth flotation
entries.world: 1905, Broken Hill; for copper 1912, Britannia, BC
entries.touches: Copper Mine & Mill, Large Copper Mine
entries.effect: copper recovered 60-75% to about 90%

entries.name: Open-pit porphyry copper
entries.effect: open-pit share of US copper 2% (1907) to 44% (1936); 88 to 259 lb of copper a man-day (1914-36)

entries.name: Chlorination
entries.effect: Toronto typhoid deaths 40.8 (1910) to 1.0 (1915) per 100,000; no separate effect found in 25 US cities

entries.name: Fat hydrogenation
entries.effect: solid fat from crops (CROPS to FATS); before, only lard and butter

entries.name: Thermal cracking
entries.effect: petrol from crude about 12-13% to about 25%; about 0.24 L of petrol a litre of gas oil (est.)

entries.name: Synthetic ammonia
entries.touches: a fertiliser works (no FERTILISER good yet; Q11)
entries.effect: nitrogen from the air; no yield figure gathered

entries.name: Moving assembly line
entries.touches: Assembly Plant; Vehicle Works, Commercial Vehicle Plant
entries.effect: 12.5 to 1.55 man-hours a chassis; Model T $850 (1909) to $290 (1925)

entries.name: Gasoline tractor
entries.touches: Grain Farm, Mixed Farm, Livestock Farm
entries.effect: replaces horses: about 3 acres of feed freed a horse; 27.3% of the US fall in farm jobs (1910-60)

entries.name: Mechanical coal loader
entries.effect: 5.5 to 8.5 short tons a man a day (one colliery, 1926); machine-loaded 0 to 31% (1939)

entries.name: Pulverised coal, high-pressure steam
entries.effect: the best plant 10,800 Btu a kWh against an average above 18,000: -40% (est.)

entries.name: Combine harvester
entries.world: 1918, prairie combine with its own engine; self-propelled 1937 (Massey-Harris)
entries.effect: wheat 40-50 to 15-20 hours per 100 bushels with PE14; 6.5 h (1955)

entries.name: Milking machine
entries.effect: cows milked an hour a milker 10 to 30

entries.name: Continuous strip mill
entries.effect: sheet about 0.5 to 8 t a man-shift (est.)

entries.name: Hybrid corn
entries.effect: yield +9% to +20%; seed bought every year

entries.name: Diesel-electric locomotive
entries.touches: Freight Line, Rail Spur, Rail Terminal; Locomotive Works
entries.effect: fuel into work 7.5% to 28%: -73% fuel a tonne-km (est.)

entries.name: Carbide cutting tools
entries.touches: Machine Works, Fabrication Shop, Fabrication Works, Vehicle Works
entries.effect: cutting speed about 4 times high-speed steel

entries.name: Delayed coking
entries.effect: residue into light products and coke (30% of its weight, the game's recipe)

entries.name: Catalytic cracking
entries.world: Jun 1936, Paulsboro (Houdry; Apr 1936 or Mar 1937 by other sources); fluid 1942
entries.effect: about 0.24 to 0.555 L of petrol a litre of gas oil fed to it; 48% gasoline at 81 octane

entries.name: Alkylation
entries.effect: cracked gas into petrol at 0.80 L a litre (the game's recipe)

entries.name: One-man chainsaw
entries.effect: 2 to up to 4 cords a worker a day

entries.name: Catalytic reforming
entries.effect: heavy naphtha into petrol at 0.82 L a litre; hydrogen for the later hydrocracker

entries.name: Pasteurised milk (a by-law)
entries.effect: about 15% of TB cases came from dairy (c.1900); infected cattle 5% (1920s) to 2% (1950). No effect on babies' deaths found in 25 US cities

entries.name: Insulin
entries.touches: a death becomes a lasting patient (as the first study's M4)
entries.effect: children with diabetes died "in a matter of months"; after, they lived on daily injections; the caseload was not found

entries.name: Diphtheria toxoid
entries.effect: Hamilton 742 cases and 32 deaths (1922) to 5 and 0 (1931); Toronto cases down at least 90% with 3 doses

entries.name: Sulfa drugs
entries.effect: US 1937-43: maternal deaths -24% to -36%, pneumonia deaths -17% to -32%, scarlet fever -52% to -65%, all deaths -2% to -3%

entries.name: Penicillin
entries.effect: gas gangrene, 150 deaths per 1,000 WWI casualties, almost gone in 1944-45. Canada, observed and not proven causal: stay 11.0 to 10.0 days (1945-50); maternal deaths 2.8 to 1.1 per 1,000 births (1944-50)

entries.name: Streptomycin
entries.touches: TB deaths among the game's long-term sick (a year or more)
entries.effect: deaths within six months 27% to 7% (MRC trial, 1946-48; unverified); Canadian TB beds kept rising until 1953

entries.name: Filling station
entries.effect: petrol from a pump instead of by the can at a store

entries.name: Self-service grocery
entries.effect: no clerk fetching each item; no delivery (about 3% of the bill) or charge account (about 2%). Posts a sale: not found
entries.feeNote: the store was patented in the US, but the first study treats business methods as free

entries.name: Supermarket
entries.effect: US supermarkets about 300 (1935) to over 15,000 (1950). Cost a sale: not found

entries.name: Workers' compensation levy (wage tax)
entries.effect: no-fault, paid by employers

entries.name: Profit tax
entries.world: Business Profits War Tax, 1916; corporate income tax, 1917
entries.effect: 25% of profits above 7% of capital (companies)

entries.name: Income tax
entries.effect: 4% above $1,500 (single) or $3,000; supertax 2% to 25%

entries.name: Minimum wage
entries.world: Manitoba and BC, 1918 (1917 by Russell), for women
entries.effect: weekly rates by trade and city

entries.name: Sales tax
entries.effect: 1% on manufacturers' and wholesalers' sales; 6% by 1923

entries.name: Zoning
entries.effect: use districts

entries.name: Old-age pensions
entries.effect: up to $20 a month at 70; income under $365; Ottawa paid half

entries.name: The central bank
entries.touches: Money: the policy rate and the currency
entries.effect: Bank Rate 2.5% (1935)

entries.name: Student aid
entries.effect: terms not found

entries.name: Unemployment insurance
entries.world: Unemployment Insurance Act, 7 Aug 1940; contributions from 1 Jul 1941
entries.effect: 9 to 36 cents a week by wage class, plus 20% from the government; benefit 34-40 times the average contribution; about 42% of workers covered

entries.name: Childcare subsidy
entries.effect: half from Ottawa (unverified)

entries.name: Public hospital insurance
entries.touches: Taxes: the health premium; Promises: care
entries.effect: Saskatchewan's premium $5 a person (unverified)

entries.name: Pension contributions (CPP)
entries.effect: 1.8% from the worker, 1.8% from the employer
